summary: Ochoco National Forest lookout whose present L-4 tower dates from 1947; the 2011 register entry says it is staffed every summer.

facts.design: Treated timber L-4 tower and cab, about 107 ft
facts.status_note: Standing and staffed each summer per the 2011 NHLR entry; no source after 2011 confirms the present state.

access.note: Forest Service lookout, staffed each summer per the 2011 register entry; no source says the cab is open to visitors.

events.note: An 18-year-old from Portland took up duties as primary lookout, on a tree platform
Ranger C.S. Congleton constructing a lookout tower on the summit (July 14, 1921 notice)
50-ft wooden tower and cabin, per firelookout.com; this date conflicts with the 1921 notice
Lookout reported one fire for the fire season
Crow's nest tree platform added 1/2 mile east, per firelookout.com
Crow's nest erected one mile east, per NHLR
Materials bought for the present tower and stored at Derr Guard Station
Present treated timber L-4 tower built (107 ft per NHLR, 108 ft per firelookout.com)
Inspection: tower and house in excellent condition, but too much sag in the cables
Registered February 9, 2011, nominated by Howard Verschoor

evidence.supports: location: Ochoco National Forest, Wheeler County, Oregon
evidence.quote:
Ochoco National Forest
Wheeler County, Oregon

evidence.supports: 1920 primary lookout on a tree platform
evidence.quote: Joe Chambreaux, a lad of eighteen from Portland, Oregon, has taken up his duties as primary lookout on Wolf Mountain which is one of the most isolated points on the Ochoco Forest.

evidence.supports: tree platform built for the lookout
evidence.quote: perched in the top of a tree on a crudely constructed platform built for the specific purpose of supporting him.

evidence.supports: 1921 Forest Service ranger building a tower on the summit
evidence.quote: Ranger C.S. Congleton, with Ed Gerow and Leon Vial helping, is constructing a lookout tower on top of Wolfe Mountain, which is about 25 miles northeast of Paulina.

Established in 1921 with a crow's nest tree platform (1/2 mile southwest of the present tower), a 50' wooden tower with 7x7' and cabin were constructed in 1926 (also 1/2 mile southwest of the present tower).
A crow's nest tree platform was added 1/2 mile east of the present tower in 1931

evidence.supports: 1932 crow's nest one mile east; wooden tower one mile west
evidence.quote: The first lookout on this site was a 50' wooden L-6 tower and cabin one mile west of the present tower. In 1932 a crow's nest was erected one mile east, which is still standing.

evidence.supports: present tower 107 ft, built 1947, staffed every summer, radio backup
evidence.quote: The present 107' treated timber L-4 tower, built in 1947, is staffed every summer and still uses the old phone system with radio backup.
1947: A 107-foot treated timber tower with an L-4 cab constructed.

evidence.supports: materials bought 1942, stored at Derr Guard Station until 1947
evidence.quote: Materials for the current 108' treated timber L-4 tower were purchased in 1942, then stored at Derr Guard Station until 1947 when enough manpower was available after World War II to build the tower.
1927: This lookout reported one fire for the fire season.
This tower and house were in excellent condition except there appeared to be too much sag in the cables.

corrections.why: 15.2 m is 50 ft, the height of the earlier wooden tower. The present L-4 tower is 107 ft per NHLR (108 ft per firelookout.com), about 32.6 m.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com dates the 50-ft wooden tower and cabin to 1926, while the 1921 notices describe a ranger constructing a tower that year. NHLR gives no date for the wooden tower. Left as a conflict.
NHLR says a crow's nest was erected in 1932; firelookout.com says a crow's nest tree platform was added in 1931.
NHLR says 107 ft and the Forest Lookouts page says 107-foot; firelookout.com says 108 ft. Stored as 32.6 m (107 ft).

notes_for_editor: Current staffing is not confirmed: the staffing statement is from the 2011 NHLR registration and firelookout.com, both undated. The access level 'restricted' is an editorial inference from the Forest Service staffing, not a source statement. The record's height_m of 15.2 appears to be the earlier wooden tower. A 2011 blog and a search summary mention a road and staffing visits, but these were not fetched, so they are not used here.
